replay_method: Re-derive order-independence from monotone fixed-assignment union, monotone source-color blocking, persistent source singletons, and monotone X0 deletion/connectivity repair. Do not use the primary proof as an assumption.

forced_assignment_union: All compared histories have exactly the same compatible forced assignment set F.
Therefore the final forced seed identities and colors are identical as sets.
seed_color_effects: For every remaining vertex, final seed-forbidden colors are the union of contributions from the old seed and adjacent assignments in F.
Union is commutative and idempotent, so source masks and source-list sizes are order-independent.
singleton_persistence: Once a source list has size one, later seed growth can only keep that same one available color or remove it and create Z0.
A nonterminal jointly reachable history cannot continue through Z0.
Hence all early singleton promotions occur with the same color in the final closure.
Every final singleton is promoted by the final canonical pass, so the final X0 promotion set is unique.
canonical_partition: Final S and X0 are unique.
Source classes are deterministic from final seed masks.
Residual Y0 is deterministic from final seed/X0 metadata.
Exact A(v) is deterministic from final fixed-color neighborhood masks.
connectivity_repair: A component deleted at some prefix is a component of G minus current X0 and has no nonfixed outside neighbor.
Every later jointly reachable forced or newly promoted vertex lies outside that component and was already nonfixed outside it at deletion time, hence has no edge into it.
Thus later forcing cannot alter the deleted component's local exact instance.
Monotone growth of X0 can split the retained seed-component but cannot reconnect deleted pieces.
Sequential deletion therefore yields the same final retained seed-component as batch deletion under final X0.
terminal_outcomes: A prefix Z0 or fixed-color conflict remains a conflict in the final combined fixed assignment state.
A P7 List-3 repair UNSAT component has no later nonfixed outside dependencies and remains an independent UNSAT obstruction.
Therefore terminal UNSAT does not depend on forcing order.
reconstruction: SAT deleted components are independent exact local obligations after deletion.
Discovery order and concrete valid local witness may differ, but the reconstruction relation factors over the same deleted vertex sets/local instances.
Canonical ordering plus deterministic local witness selection yields a normalized receipt if byte-level identity is desired.
downstream: C0, C2, B2A and C3 are recomputed from the final canonical graph/fixed sets/component data and are therefore order-independent.
